spec.description: Live network performance of the embedded monitor (Raspberry Pi 5). Shows latency, packet loss and reachability (ping), with throughput, Wi-Fi signal, interface traffic, TCP fallback and path (traceroute) to be added. Data: VictoriaMetrics on the Pi, pushed by src/scheduler.py every 30 s. EEE4022S, UCT.

spec.title: Latency (RTT)
spec.description: round-trip time to 8.8.8.8 from 5 pings every 10 s: avg = average, min = fastest reply, max = slowest reply. a high max with a normal avg means one slow reply.

spec.title: Ping time now
spec.description: The round-trip time to 8.8.8.8, average of 5 pings, every 10 s. lower is better.

spec.title: Packet loss now
spec.description: The 5 pings to 8.8.8.8 that got no reply in the latest check (steps of 20 %). 0 % is normal.

spec.title: Download use now
spec.description: The 10 mbit/s reference download link (inethi) in use now, from snmp every 10 s. yellow from 50 %, red from 70 %. includes the monitor’s own iperf3 tests. on eduroam it can go above 100 %, because eduroam is faster than the reference.

spec.title: Upload use now
spec.description: The 5 mbit/s reference upload link (inethi) in use now, from snmp every 10 s. yellow from 50 %, red from 70 %. includes the monitor’s own iperf3 tests. on eduroam it can go above 100 %.

spec.title: Backhaul up (time range)
spec.description: The checks in the chosen time range where the internet link was up. local link down and unknown count as not up. times when the monitor was not running are not counted.

spec.title: Backhaul state over time
spec.description: History of the internet link (backhaul): green = up, red = down, orange = the pi’s own wi-fi was off, grey = not checked yet.

spec.title: Download speed
spec.description: download through the pi’s wi-fi (wlan0), from snmp every 10 s. dashed lines: 5 mbit/s (yellow, 50 %) and 7 mbit/s (red, 70 %) of the 10 mbit/s inethi reference

spec.title: Upload speed
spec.description: Upload through the pi’s wi-fi (wlan0), from snmp every 10 s. dashed lines: 2.5 mbit/s (yellow, 50 %) and 3.5 mbit/s (red, 70 %) of the 5 mbit/s inethi reference.

spec.title: Link full (1 minute)
spec.description: red = the link was full for at least 1 whole minute (≥ 70 % of the inethi reference: 7 mbit/s down, 3.5 mbit/s up). short bursts are not shown. check the iperf3 panel below: our own tests can also fill the link.

spec.title: Monitor's own iperf3 tests
spec.description: purple = the monitor’s own speed test (iperf3) was running. it fills the link for about 10 s per test, 4 times a day, so traffic and “full” blocks at the same time are caused by the monitor, not by users.

spec.title: Packet loss
spec.description: Percentage of 5 ICMP packets to $target that got no reply, per measurement (steps of 20 %).

spec.title: TCP speed (iperf3)
spec.description: Highest speed the link carried during the monitor’s iperf3 test (10 s each way), up to 4 times a day. night = link capacity; day = speed left over while people use the link.

spec.title: UDP jitter
spec.description: How much the delay between packets varied during the 10 s udp test at 500 kbit/s (measured by the server). lower is better.

spec.title: UDP loss
spec.description: The udp packets that did not arrive during the 10 s test (505 packets). 0 % is normal.

spec.title: Latest iperf3 set
spec.description: Results of the newest speed test set (last 24 h): one row per test. udp has no retransmits; tcp has no jitter or loss, so those cells are empty.

spec.title: Latency variation (mdev)
spec.description: How much the 5 ping reply times differed in each check (every 10 s). near 0 = steady link; high = unsteady (jitter). use with the netem jitter test.

spec.title: TCP check
spec.description: Runs only when ping gets no reply: a tcp connection to 1.1.1.1:443 (another company than the ping target). green = the link works, ping was only blocked. red = the link really failed. empty = ping was fine, no check needed.

spec.title: Traceroute result
spec.description: Shows if the path to 8.8.8.8 worked and where it broke. runs when the backhaul goes down, every 30 min while down, when it comes back, and once an hour as a normal baseline. “pi cannot reach gateway” = the problem is the pi’s own first hop.

spec.title: last hop that replied
spec.description: Number of the last router on the path to 8.8.8.8 that replied. normal = 10-11 (8.8.8.8 itself). a lower number during an outage shows where along the path the replies stopped.

spec.title: Latest path (hop by hop)
spec.description: The routers on the way to 8.8.8.8 from the latest traceroute (last hour): hop number, router ip and reply time per probe. hops that did not answer (* * *) are not listed. per-hop times are only a hint: routers answer traceroute at low priority.

spec.title: Wi-Fi signal strength
spec.description: Signal strength the pi receives from its access point, measured every 2 s. closer to 0 is stronger (e.g. -50 dBm is better than -75 dBm). a sudden drop or gap can explain loss or a local link down.

spec.title: Wi-Fi connected?
spec.description: Is the pi connected to its wi-fi access point? checked every 2 s. red = the pi’s own wi-fi was down, so the internet link could not be checked (local link down), not a backhaul failure.

spec.title: Which access point (BSSID)
spec.description: Which wi-fi access point the pi was connected to. each row is one access point (its bssid). a change from one row to another = the pi moved to another access point; a drop at the same time can explain a local link down.

spec.title: Wi-Fi channel (frequency)
spec.description: Rdio frequency the pi uses to talk to its access point. a step up or down = the access point changed channel; devices can briefly drop when that happens.

spec.title: Wi-Fi link rate
spec.description: The speed the pi’s radio and the access point agreed to use (from iw), every 2 s. it shows radio quality, not internet speed: the real internet speed is in the throughput tab.

spec.title: Status timeline
spec.description: Result of each ping check (5 pings to 8.8.8.8 every 10 s). no reply = nothing came back. ping error = ping itself reported a problem, e.g. “network is unreachable” when the pi’s wi-fi is off.

spec.title: Ping Errors
spec.description: Errors table, which shows the error messages.

spec.title: Backhaul now
spec.description: Internet link (backhaul) status

spec.title: Network Monitor
